comments.body:
## RCA — root cause PROVEN at runtime (not the reported hypothesis)

The ticket's own hypothesis was "the MCP server is launched from a global/stale Python env
that lacks the `[agents]` Bedrock extra". That is **wrong in an important way**: there is no
stale env, and `[agents]` has never carried Bedrock. The server runs from a container whose
dependency set is built exactly as specified — and the specification omits the provider.

### The mechanism

1. `pyproject.toml:131` — `[agents]` is `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries,duckduckgo]>=1.107,<2`.
   It carries **no** bedrock support, by design.
2. `pyproject.toml:142-144` — `[bedrock]` is a **separate, opt-in** extra
   (`pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]>=1,<2`). The split is deliberate: commit `747e14945593`
   (ticket 2932) states "boto3 stays out of the default install: `[agents]` is unchanged and
   the new `[bedrock]` extra is opt-in, with dev carrying it".
3. `pyproject.toml:213+` — `[dev]` pulls boto3/botocore, which is why the repo `.venv` works
   and masked this in every local session.
4. `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:43` — the deployed image builds with
   `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp`. **No `--extra bedrock`, and
   `--no-dev`**, so the container has neither source of the provider.
5. `rebar.toml:198-199` — the configured model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`.
   Because the container sets `REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`, config discovery is
   rooted there (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:74-104`, `:188-217`), and that clone carries
   this same `rebar.toml` — so the Bedrock model IS read.
6. `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:127-139` — the provider builder imports
   `pydantic_ai.providers.bedrock` lazily and raises the named `LLMConfigError` when absent.
   That is the exact string the ticket reports.

So: a Bedrock model is configured, the Bedrock provider package is not installed, the LLM
layer cannot start, `review_plan` degrades to the deterministic floor and returns an unsigned
`INDETERMINATE` with `llm_unavailable` — minting no attestation.

### Discriminating experiment (runtime, not static)

Two interpreters, **identical code, identical `LLMConfig`** (`model="bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8"`,
`bedrock_region_name="us-east-1"`), differing only in installed extras:

- venv built as `[agents,mcp]` (the image's exact extras):
  `LLMConfigError: a bedrock model/provider is configured but the optional bedrock provider package is not installed: pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]'`
  — **byte-identical to the reported `llm_error`**.
- venv built as `[dev]` (has bedrock): `BUILT OK: BedrockProvider`.

This rules out the live alternatives: config-not-discovered (config was passed explicitly and
identically to both), missing credentials and missing region (both supplied; neither is
reached — the failure is at import), and model-string/provider-qualifier parsing (identical
input to both).

**Note on Acceptance Criterion 1:** its proposed check,
`importlib.util.find_spec('pydantic_ai.models.bedrock')`, is a **weak oracle and would have
passed on the broken container**. Measured in the container-equivalent venv: the module file
ships with `pydantic-ai-slim` unconditionally, so `find_spec` is truthy while `boto3` is
`None`. The failure is raised on *import*, not on spec lookup. A correct probe imports the
provider (or probes `boto3`).

### Defect attribution

`caused_by` -> **fd4a-4e91-f179-4932** (commit `8297083532a3`, 2026-08-24, "Add rebar-mcp HTTP
service to the AWS box"), the change that introduced `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` and its
`uv sync` line.

This is deliberately **not** attributed as an unmet obligation against the Bedrock cutover.
The obligation ("this repo's configured provider is Bedrock") was created on **2026-08-03** by
commit `5bc3a432d728` (ticket d2ce, "default local dev to Bedrock"), which added
`[llm] model = "bedrock:..."` to `rebar.toml`. `Dockerfile.mcp` arrived **three weeks later**,
on 2026-08-24, with the Bedrock config already in the tree — so it is the later change, it was
authored against the obligation, and its reviewer could plausibly have caught the omission.
The date test therefore points at fd4a, not d2ce.

Close class: `plan_defect` — the image's dependency specification was wrong at authoring time,
not broken later by someone else.

### Legitimacy: `defect` (cited)

`docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md:98` designs this server to mint **both** op-cert kinds
("plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close"), and `Dockerfile.mcp:36` declares the
`agents` extra to be "the rebar.llm gate runtime the certified tools drive", with compose
setting `REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM=1`. An image that cannot start the configured provider cannot
mint a plan-review op-cert, so it violates a cited design contract.

### Second, independent gap found on the same surface (would make the fix fail differently)

Adding the extra alone is **not sufficient** for the deployed server. The `mcp` compose
service (`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:319+`) and the blue-green
`mcp_run_new` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:367-396`) set **no AWS region at all**, while the
sibling `review-bot` service sets both `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` and `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`
with a MEASURED comment (`docker-compose.yml:143-162`, ticket a574) recording that
in-container `boto3.session.Session().region_name` is `None` and bedrock-runtime construction
raises `NoRegionError` — and that this is independent of IMDS, which resolves fine (ticket
9249). `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:160-173` is the corresponding no-region raise.

### Credentials / region finding (verified read-only against AWS, not assumed)

- Instance `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` is in **us-east-1**, instance profile
  `rebar-gerrit-instance-profile` -> role `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`.
- That role carries inline policy `rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse`, allowing
  `bedrock:InvokeModel` + `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on
  `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*` and
  `arn:aws:bedrock:*:896586841071:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`.

So **credentials and permissions are already in place** and reach the container via the
instance role. Region is the gap, and it is a config/env gap, not a credential one.

## Fix landed locally (NOT pushed) — ticket deliberately left OPEN pending live validation

Commit `443609b8989de8391b44a813ca91b6b2a4a30a47` on worktree branch `d43e-bedrock-extra`
(`/Users/joeoakhart/d43e-bedrock-extra`), signed off, trailer verified
(`rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev HEAD` -> OK).

### What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` | `uv sync … --extra agents --extra mcp` -> `… --extra bedrock` (the root cause) |
| `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` | `mcp` service gains `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` + `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` = `us-east-1` |
| `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` | `mcp_run_new` gains the same two `-e` flags (the path a real deploy takes) |
| `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` | +3 guards (coupling + two parity), 153 lines |

`[agents]` and `[bedrock]` are kept SEPARATE rather than flattened. Checked the history first:
the split is deliberate (ticket sporadic-bratty-porcupine — "boto3 stays out of the default
install"), and `[agents]` is what every PyPI consumer of `nava-rebar` installs, so folding
boto3 in would tax every non-Bedrock adopter to fix one deployment. `Dockerfile.reviewbot` had
already made exactly this declaration on 2026-08-03, three weeks before `Dockerfile.mcp` was
authored — which is also why the attribution lands on fd4a-4e91-f179-4932 rather than on the
Bedrock cutover.

### RED -> GREEN -> mutation

- **RED** (before fix): all three new tests fail. The coupling guard's message names the gap
  precisely — "Dockerfile.mcp installs extras ['agents', 'mcp'], which cannot serve every
  provider configured in rebar.toml (['anthropic', 'bedrock']): missing extra(s) ['bedrock']".
- **GREEN** (after fix): `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` 30 passed.
- **Mutation** (sandboxed under `sandbox-exec`, writes denied outside the worktree): each of
  the three changes re-removed individually returns exactly its own test to RED, and restoring
  returns all 30 to green.
- **Coupling mutation**: re-pointing `rebar.toml` at `openai:gpt-4o` with the Dockerfile
  UNTOUCHED also fails the guard — so it is a genuine config<->image coupling check, not a
  string match on the `uv sync` line.
- **Dependency-level replication of the original report**: a venv built with the image's OLD
  extras `[agents,mcp]` raises the reported error verbatim; one built with the NEW extras
  `[agents,mcp,bedrock]` returns `BUILT OK: BedrockProvider`.

### Gates

`make lint` exit 0 (incl. the shrink-only complexity ratchet: `new=0 increased=0`),
`make typecheck` exit 0 (678 files), `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` 4 passed (no
`src/rebar` file touched, so the 800-LOC CI gate is unaffected), and the FULL unit suite
**14009 passed, 51 skipped** — no regressions.

`rebar review-plan` on this ticket: **PASS, signed** (0 blocking, 1 advisory, 1 coaching;
`llm_ran: true`, `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`, attested at
`97b003c4cd0e0d448595d87e994e5999fedee7f5`). Run through the LOCAL repo `.venv` CLI — which is
the whole point of this bug: the same op through the deployed MCP server still cannot run.

### Provider audit against the operator directive ("Bedrock for ALL")

- Every gate YAML binds model **CLASSES**, not bare ids (`plan-review.yaml`, `code-review.yaml`),
  and `rebar.toml`'s class table points all three at Bedrock. Good.
- **Every built-in default is direct-Anthropic**: `DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"`
  (`src/rebar/llm/config.py:65`), `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4-6"` (`:71`),
  `TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-4-5"` (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:45`), and any
  bare `claude*` infers `anthropic` (`config.py:179-187`). These only fire if the config is not
  discovered — and `_read_llm_file_table` SWALLOWS a `ConfigError` and degrades to `{}`
  (`config.py:369-372`), so an unreadable `rebar.toml` in the container would silently serve
  every class from direct Anthropic rather than failing closed. Recorded as residual risk below.
- **`rebar.toml:209-210` gives `frontier` and `standard` direct-`anthropic:` fallbacks**, and
  `should_fall_back` (`model_classes.py:366-393`) uses them on availability errors. The
  container also receives a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `.env`
  (`infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh:210`), so that arm is LIVE. **NOT changed** — `rebar.toml:181-187`
  records an explicit operator decision (2026-08-07) that this arm is approved, and the table is
  repo-wide, so editing it would change local dev and CI too. **Operator decision required** if
  the deployed server is to be Bedrock-only.
- Two non-class residual paths ride the scalar `cfg.model`: `spec_scan.py:127` and
  `overlap/digest_sidecar.py:151-157`. `rebar.toml:198` sets that scalar to Bedrock, so they
  are correct today, but they are the paths that would fall to `DEFAULT_MODEL` if config
  discovery failed.

### Credentials / region (verified read-only against AWS, not assumed)

Instance `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` is in **us-east-1**, profile `rebar-gerrit-instance-profile` ->
role `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`, which carries inline policy `rebar-gerrit-bedrock-converse`
allowing `bedrock:InvokeModel` + `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` on
`arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*` and
`arn:aws:bedrock:*:896586841071:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*`. **Credentials and
permissions are already in place**; no operator action needed there. Region was the gap and is
now set explicitly in both deploy paths.

### Sibling sweep (Step 7)

- **Axis 1 (construct).** `Dockerfile.reviewbot` already declares `--extra bedrock` — correct.
  `Dockerfile.opcert:39` does **not**, yet `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:68-76` dispatches
  the real `review_plan`/`verify_completion`. It is not currently broken only because
  `reviewbot = [..., "boto3"]` satisfies the provider INCIDENTALLY — precisely the latent
  accident `Dockerfile.reviewbot`'s own comment warns about. **Filed as
  atrophied-unbeatable-hermitcrab (e46b-9ca3-d1b3-4dd4)**, linked `discovered_from` this bug,
  with file impact set. Not fixed in scope: it is a different service, not currently failing,
  and the operator directive was scoped to the MCP instance.
- **Axis 2 (parity).** Surfaces for this operation are Dockerfile / compose service /
  autodeploy `docker run`. All three are now covered: the extra in the Dockerfile, and region
  in BOTH compose and `mcp_run_new` (compose-only would never have reached a deployed
  container). `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml` is the CI matrix arm, N/A here.

### Residual risk (observed, dispositioned)

- **ACCEPTED / operator call:** the direct-Anthropic fallback arm above.
- **ACCEPTED, worth a ticket if you want it:** there is **no startup preflight** for the
  configured provider. `_capabilities.py:100-107` defines a `bedrock_provider` capability with
  an ERROR posture, but neither `require_capability` nor `is_available` is called anywhere in
  `src/` for it — the only `guard_import` call site in the tree is
  `metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py:30`. So a misconfigured container starts CLEAN and
  fails only at first gate invocation, which is exactly why this bug reached production
  silently. A boot-time capability check would have failed the container closed instead.
- **ACCEPTED:** `_read_llm_file_table` swallowing `ConfigError` into `{}` (`config.py:369-372`)
  means an unreadable config degrades to direct-Anthropic defaults rather than failing closed.

### Why this ticket is NOT being closed

Acceptance criterion 2 as originally written is a **live-validation** criterion: "`review_plan`
via the MCP server … returns `coverage.llm_ran = true` … and `signature.signed = true` —
checked by re-running the tool and inspecting the returned JSON." That can only be observed
against the **deployed** server, which requires the operator to land this change and redeploy.
Nothing in this session can honestly tick it, so the ticket stays `in_progress`.

**Operator next steps:** land `443609b8989d` through Gerrit, redeploy the mcp service, then
re-run `review_plan` through the MCP server and confirm `llm_ran: true` / `signed: true`. Note
the criterion's own suggested probe (`find_spec('pydantic_ai.models.bedrock')`) is a WEAK
oracle and would have passed on the broken container — measured, that module ships with
`pydantic-ai-slim` unconditionally and is truthy while `boto3` is absent. Probe `boto3`, or
import the provider.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The deployed `rebar` **MCP server**'s `review_plan` cannot run its LLM passes: the container
has no AWS Bedrock provider package, while the configured model is a Bedrock model. The review
degrades to the deterministic floor and returns an unsigned `INDETERMINATE`, so **no
plan-review attestation is minted** and the claim gate cannot be satisfied through the MCP
surface — even though the repo `.venv` has the provider and the local CLI reviews fine.

Observed via a live `review_plan` call on 2026-08-27 (on story `6f74-2795-5ad4-4a56`):

```
"verdict": "INDETERMINATE",
"coverage": { "llm_ran": false, "llm_unavailable": true,
  "llm_error": "a bedrock model/provider is configured but the optional bedrock provider
   package is not installed: pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock]'" },
"signature": { "signed": false, "reason": "INDETERMINATE" }
```

Expected: the four-pass LLM review runs and, on a non-blocking PASS, signs a plan-review
attestation — the behaviour `docs/adr/0104-mcp-on-box.md:98` designs this server for ("the two
op-cert kinds minted via MCP: plan-review at claim, completion-verifier at close").

## Root cause — PROVEN, and NOT the originally filed hypothesis

The filed hypothesis was "the server runs from a stale/global interpreter lacking the
`[agents]` Bedrock extra". Disproved: there is no stale env, and `[agents]` has never carried
Bedrock. The server runs from the compose-built container, whose dependency set is exactly what
`Dockerfile.mcp` specifies — and that specification omits the configured provider.

- `pyproject.toml:131` — `[agents]` is `pydantic-ai-slim[anthropic,retries,duckduckgo]`; no bedrock.
- `pyproject.toml:142-144` — `[bedrock]` is a **separate opt-in** extra, deliberately split so
  boto3 stays out of the lean default install (ticket sporadic-bratty-porcupine).
- `pyproject.toml:213+` — `[dev]` carries boto3, which is why the repo `.venv` works and
  masked this in every local session.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp:43` — the image builds with
  `uv sync --locked --no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp`. No `--extra bedrock`, and `--no-dev`,
  so neither source of the provider is present.
- `rebar.toml:198-199` — configured model is `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, and the
  container's `REBAR_ROOT` roots config discovery at a clone carrying that same file.
- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py:127-139` raises the named `LLMConfigError` on the lazy import.

Discriminating runtime experiment (full detail in the RCA comment): two interpreters, identical
code and identical `LLMConfig`, differing only in installed extras. `[agents,mcp]` raises the
reported error byte-for-byte; `[dev]` builds a `BedrockProvider`. This rules out
config-not-discovered, missing credentials, missing region, and model-string parsing.

Attributed `caused_by` **fd4a-4e91-f179-4932**, the change that introduced `Dockerfile.mcp`
three weeks AFTER the Bedrock config already existed. Close class `plan_defect`.

## Second gap on the same surface (the fix fails differently without it)

The `mcp` compose service and `mcp_run_new` in `autodeploy.sh` set **no AWS region**, while the
sibling `review-bot` service sets two, with a MEASURED comment (`docker-compose.yml`, ticket
a574) that in-container `boto3.session.Session().region_name` is `None` and bedrock-runtime
raises `NoRegionError` — independently of IMDS, which resolves. Credentials themselves are
fine: instance `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` (us-east-1) carries role `rebar-gerrit-instance-role`
with an inline `bedrock:InvokeModel` policy on `anthropic.claude-*`.

## Fix plan

**1. `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp`** — add `--extra bedrock` to the locked install. Keep
`[agents]` and `[bedrock]` separate rather than flattening: the split is deliberate, and
`[agents]` is what every PyPI consumer of `nava-rebar` installs, so folding boto3 in would tax
every non-Bedrock adopter to fix one deployment. The lock already covers it (`uv sync --locked
--no-dev --extra agents --extra mcp --extra bedrock --dry-run` exits 0).

**2. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`** (`mcp` service) — add `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` and
`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, both `us-east-1`, matching the review-bot's already-proven posture. The
two are not interchangeable: rebar's knob threads into `BedrockProvider` and is recorded in the
signed verdict's provenance; `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` is what a bare boto3 caller reads.

**3. `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`** (`mcp_run_new`) — the same two `-e` flags. This is the path
a real deploy takes, so compose-only vars would never reach a container.

**4. `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py`** — RED-first guards, in that file's existing
image/compose-contract style: a **coupling** guard that parses `rebar.toml`'s configured
providers (via rebar's own `infer_provider`, so it cannot drift from the resolver) and asserts
the image installs an extra able to serve each; plus region parity for compose and autodeploy.

## Explicitly OUT of scope — operator decision, reported not changed

`rebar.toml:209-210` gives the `frontier` and `standard` classes direct-`anthropic:` fallbacks,
and `should_fall_back` (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:366-393`) uses them on an availability
error; the container also receives a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` via `.env`. So a non-Bedrock
provider is reachable. Not removed here: `rebar.toml:181-187` records an explicit operator
decision (2026-08-07, ticket 2876) that this arm is approved, and the table is repo-wide, so
editing it changes local dev and CI too. Making the deployed server Bedrock-only is a scope
decision, not a bug fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp` installs the `bedrock` extra alongside `agents` and `mcp`,
      and the committed lock resolves that set (`uv sync --locked … --dry-run` exits 0).
- [ ] The `mcp` compose service and `mcp_run_new` each set `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION` and
      `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` to the instance's region, and the two agree.
- [ ] A test in `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` fails when the image's extras cannot
      serve every provider configured in `rebar.toml`, and passes once the extra is added;
      shown RED before the fix and killed by re-removing the extra (mutation).
- [ ] Tests assert region parity between the compose `mcp` service and `mcp_run_new`.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py` and
      `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py` all pass.
- [ ] The recurrence guard is recorded where it is enforced, not only in prose: the image's
      extras are coupled to the configured providers by an executable test, and
      `Dockerfile.mcp` states why the bedrock extra is required.
- [ ] LIVE VALIDATION (requires the operator to land and deploy): `review_plan` through the
      deployed MCP server returns `coverage.llm_ran = true` with no `llm_unavailable`, and on a
      non-blocking PASS `signature.signed = true`. NOTE the criterion originally proposed here
      (`find_spec('pydantic_ai.models.bedrock')`) is a WEAK oracle — measured, that module ships
      with `pydantic-ai-slim` unconditionally and is truthy even with `boto3` absent, so it
      would have passed on the broken container. Probe `boto3`, or import the provider.

file_impact.reason: add --extra bedrock to the uv sync line so the configured Bedrock provider package is installed in the deployed image (the proven root cause)
set REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION and AWS_DEFAULT_REGION on the mcp service, at parity with the review-bot service, so the Bedrock provider has a resolvable region in-container
pass the same two region vars in mcp_run_new so the blue-green docker run stays at parity with compose
RED-first guards: couple the image extras to the providers configured in rebar.toml, and assert mcp region parity across compose and autodeploy
